definition-changed.flag: class | of a data item; interface | of an object
definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 (4.34) defines class of a data item by PICTURE/USAGE, a predefined identifier or an intrinsic function, as 2023 3.33 does in its note; this rule's 'class' is the object-oriented class (4.33/4.36), not a data class, so the difference reaches nothing the rule governs. The rule places the working-storage section by source-element kind (class, factory, instance, method, interface definition); none of the kinds rests on the interface-of-an-object definition.

definition-dropped.flag: class definition | in object orientation (newer: undefined); method (newer: 9.3.4)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 (4.36) 'A compilation unit that defines a class of objects' is word for word 2023 3.35 (the screen's 'newer: undefined' is a miss: 2023 still defines it), so the class definitions the rule reaches are the same. §2002:4 (4.121) method 'A procedural entity defined by a method definition within, or inherited by, a class definition' names the same entity 2023 describes in 9.3.4; the method definitions the rule places or refuses are the same source elements.

pending-clause.answer: Read §2002:9.3.5: 2002 binds an invocation by method-name alone (2023 9.3.6 adds signature matching); this rule is a placement or structure rule triggered by the word 'method' and involves no invocation or binding, so it does not rest on the changed text.
